title: Are Noise-Resilient Logical Timers Useful for Performance Analysis?
problem: Performance measurements in modern HPC systems suffer from noise, and repeating measurements for statistical confidence is prohibitively expensive. This paper investigates whether logical clock-based measurements can provide noise-resilient performance analysis without multiple runs.
motivation: Noise-resilient measurement techniques are critical for efficient performance analysis in large-scale HPC systems where re-experimentation is costly.
method: The authors implement a logical clock in Score-P that increments based on computational work rather than real-time. They investigate three clock increment strategies: OpenMP loop iteration counting, LLVM basic block/statement counting, and hardware counter integration. The approach is evaluated using Score-P and Scalasca trace analysis tools on MPI+OpenMP mini-applications.
key_novelty: Logical clock implementation in Score-P that provides noise-resilient performance measurements by tracking computational work rather than elapsed time.
contributions: Logical clock mechanism in Score-P independent of real-time measurements for noise resilience
Three computational work modeling strategies: OpenMP loop iteration, LLVM basic block/statement, and hardware counter-based counting
Comprehensive evaluation of strengths (reliable detection of algorithmic issues and load imbalance) and limitations (inability to capture memory contention)
Characterization of logical time-based measurements as a specialized but valuable performance analysis tool

metrics.other: Effectiveness at detecting algorithmic performance issues and load imbalance

limitations: Logical time-based measurements cannot capture external aspects of program execution such as memory contention and environmental factors.
